items.anchor: On a compact sublevel, finite convexity bounds the gradients
items.note: New on 16 October 2026 (M42). Exact existing statement: for any finite convex F and compact K, every subgradient at every x∈K is uniformly bounded in Euclidean norm (BfgsCoverage.Companion.Ch02M.bounded_subgradients). Actual gradients at differentiability points are subgradients by the convex supporting inequality. This needs no certificate or planar-switching assumption. The article uses the same fact in A/energy/proof/005.

items.anchor: Armijo makes the predicted decreases summable.
items.note: New on 16 October 2026 (M42). The compact-sublevel premise is inherited from the beginning of the same sentence, together with the admissible-run convention. summability_stronger gives ∑d_k<∞ on a compact initial sublevel; if a larger compact sublevel contains the start, the closed initial sublevel is a compact subset. No unconditional Armijo summability without a lower objective bound is asserted.
